Riley (Customer): Hey, we're seeing intermittent 403s from our prod service since yesterday evening. Some requests succeed, others fail. Very high variance. Anyone seen this pattern?
Kai Support: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste an example curl or SDK call that fails? Also which endpoints — /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings, rerank?
Riley (Customer): Mostly during the batch job that does embeddings + rerank in sequence. Embeddings calls always OK. Rerank/generation calls occasionally 403 with body: `{\"error\":{\"message\":\"insufficient_permissions\",\"code\":403}}`.
Riley (Customer): We use a service key provisioned via SSO, looks like OIDC flow from our IdP. Our engineering team didn't change anything.
Kai Support: Got it. Can you run a quick repro with curl showing headers? e.g. `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" `
Kai Support:     -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
Kai Support:     -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate
Riley (Customer): Pasting log snippet (sanitized):
Riley (Customer): ```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 02:17:23 GMT
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":{"message":"insufficient_permissions: missing scope 'inference.generate'","code":403}}
```
Kai Support: That message is helpful — it looks like the key is missing the inference/generation permission, while embeddings permission exists which explains why embeddings succeed.
Maya CS: Riley, do you know if the key is an org-wide key or a project/service key? SSO provisioners sometimes create read-only or embeddings-only keys depending on the role mapping.
Riley (Customer): It's a service key generated by our SSO provisioning flow. We asked for "llm-service" role. Not sure what scopes that maps to.
Omar Eng: @Riley can you paste the result of the token-introspect endpoint? You can use: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.dev/v1/token/introspect`
Omar Eng: That should return scopes included on the token. (We only log non-sensitive fields)
Riley (Customer): Introspect returned: `scopes: ["embeddings.create","rerank.read"]` — aha, no `inference.generate`.
Kai Support: There it is. Looks like role mapping dropped the generate permission. Two likely culprits: (1) your IdP role-to-scope mapping changed, (2) the SSO provisioning template created a limited service key.
Kai Support: Quick mitigation: create a new API key from Console -> Developer -> API keys and select the 'inference' + 'embeddings' checkboxes, or ask your org admin to update the provisioning template to include `inference.generate` and `rerank.write` as needed.
Riley (Customer): Is there a way to check which keys were provisioned by SSO vs manually? We have dozens.
Maya CS: In Console -> Audit logs you can filter for `event:api_key.created` and `source:ssoprovisioner` — that'll show SSO-created keys. Also token names often include the service name.
Omar Eng: For a short-term workaround if you can't update SSO mapping immediately: create a scoped org key with the needed scopes and rotate the service to use it. Make sure to grant least privilege.
Riley (Customer): Will do. One more question — why does rerank sometimes succeed if rerank scope is `rerank.read`? Some reranks in our pipeline are served by the embeddings-only endpoint + client-side ranking, others call Redwood /v1/rerank.
Kai Support: If you use embeddings -> client-side ranking, that path only needs embeddings scope. The `/v1/rerank` server-side endpoint requires `rerank.write` (or `rerank.execute` depending on name). In your introspect you had `rerank.read` which might allow status/list but not execute. So some jobs that used client-side logic passed, server-side rerank failed.
Riley (Customer): Ok makes sense. We'll provision a new key and test. Any tips to validate before rotating across prod?
Omar Eng: Yes — run these checks with the new key in staging first: 1) `curl /v1/embeddings` 2) `curl /v1/generate` 3) `curl /v1/rerank` and verify 200s. Also run `curl /v1/token/introspect` and confirm scopes contain `embeddings.create`, `inference.generate`, `rerank.write`.
Kai Support: Also watch Console->Requests for 401/403 spikes and set a short TTL on the new key until you confirm. If you hit any unexpected failures, ping this thread and tag @Maya CS and @Omar Eng and we'll escalate. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Deploy job #8421 finished — no infra changes to auth layer detected in timeframe.
Riley (Customer): Thanks all — creating a new scoped key now, will post results in 15m.
Riley (Customer): Update: new key fixed the failures, all generator and rerank calls return 200. No regressions seen. Thanks for the quick triage! :raised_hands:
